newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Foreigners back strong Bucharest bourse show.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners back strong Bucharest bourse show.

text.p: New Romanian portfolio legislation prompted foreign investors to rush to buy stocks on the Bucharest bourse this week, when turnover, helped by special deals, climbed to record highs two days in a row.
"There is heavy foreign interest in Romanian equities after government commitments to regulate the market," a broker said. "The record turnover levels of the past two days are proof."

Brokers said prospects of big foreign capital inflows were in store. Turnover hit an all-time high of 65.5 billion lei ($9.2 million) on Thursday. That was more than twice the previous record of 25.9 billion -- set the day before.
The highs were triggered by special deals in first-tier chemical plant Oltchim and fertiliser maker Azomures, which traders said drew in foreign interest.
"The specials showed there were holders of large packages and that there was interest in those packages at the other end," Creditanstalt Securities president Marcel Cobuz said.

"What happened on the bourse this week was the prelude to a mass flow of foreign portfolio investment. Foreigners may have taken heart from recent developments which show a politically stable Romania."

The centrist government, which won last November's elections and ended seven years of rule by ex-communists, this week announced a 1.5 percent tax on each portfolio transaction. That amended previously proposed rules setting a four percent fee on capital gains repatriation.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's authority has been enhanced in the past week when the government easily survived two opposition confidence motions in parliament.

It has also gained in credibility for its consistency in carrying out shock-therapy reforms after seven years of what both Romanian and Western analysts regard as a half-hearted approach to market change.

Traders were split in their view of the new investment rules. Some said the new tax was punitive and would diminish flows into the market, while others argued that the market had sufficient potential to render the fee bearable.
"Foreigner portfolio investors seemed to have accepted the new tax as a feature of an emerging market, something they have to assume the way they assume hard currency risk," Cobuz said.
Thursday's four special trades -- deals struck outside the market and reported to the stock exchange later -- involved a total 22.3 million shares worth more than 49 billion lei.
Some brokers blamed specials for depressing stock prices. "Such deals are struck outside the market and therefore their price is not the market quote," said one.
But others defended such market instruments, saying they actually helped reinvigorate bourse performance. "They are made at lower prices as they involve large volumes," a trader said.

The special deals on Thursday were struck at 2,400 to 2,500 lei per share for Azomures, compared to a best market bid of 3,450 lei per share. For Oltchim, the share price in the deals was 2,100 lei, compared to a best bid of 3,400.
Bourse officials and analysts said the record levels were prompted not only by the new legislation but by other factors showing the government meant business with privatisation and other reforms.
"The State Ownership Fund (FPS) announced the selloff of 60 firms at the bourse, which boosted confidence in higher market liquidity in future," bourse official Adriana Tanasoiu said.
The FPS has a control stake in most Romanian companies.
"The overall image of the Bucharest bourse now is one of a market which performs well, registering spectacular developments from day to day," Cobuz said. ($ = 7135 Romanian Lei)
